title: Historic Deal Positions FIA World Endurance Championship for Record Decade of Growth as the Sport Enters its Golden Age
summary: Sport news The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide, and the Automobile Club de l’Ouest (ACO), the founder and organiser of the 24 Hours of Le Mans, have today announced a major deal for the FIA World Endurance Championship (FIA WEC), securing another decade of growth.   The landmark agreement, which comes during a period of unprecedented growth for the championship, will ensure a common ambition to expand the partnership and drive its commercial success. It will run from the end of 2027, when the current agreement expires, to the end of 2037.    Under the extended partnership agreement, all regulatory processes will be overseen by FIA Working Groups, the FIA Endurance Commission, and will require the final approval of the FIA World Motor Sport Council. The homologation process has also been streamlined, with the FIA and ACO overseeing the homologation of all cars competing in the Hypercar class.   The renewed partnership will also deliver significantly increased branding for the FIA. This includes enhanced branding prominently displayed across key areas including parc fermé, the podium and the Safety Cars, as well as across broadcast coverage.   With an expanding fanbase, a wider pool of competitors, and a global calendar of iconic events, the championship is stronger than ever. Since its inception in 2012, it has set the global standard for long-distance circuit racing. Following the introduction of the Hypercar regulations in 2021, interest in the championship from motor sport fans and from the automotive world has surged.    FIA WEC’s trackside audience has grown 8% so far in 2026, with millions of fans following the championship globally. The fanbase for the championship is also evolving. This year, 44% of attendees are aged 34 or younger, while 40% are attending an FIA WEC event for the first time. The championship has secured the long-term loyalty of its existing fanbase, while building the next generation of endurance racing fans.   Eight of the world’s leading auto-manufacturers currently compete in Hypercar, the top category of FIA WEC. Following the addition of the LMGT3 class in 2024, the championship now counts no fewer than 14 marques in total on the starting grid. Two more giants of the automotive industry – Ford and McLaren – are set to join the Hypercar ranks in 2027.   For over 100 years, endurance racing has served as a proven testbed for technologies that transfer from track to road. This renewed agreement creates a solid framework for advancing hydrogen powertrains in competition, providing a clear pathway toward more sustainable transport and mobility.    It will also deliver a more unified technical framework that defines top-level endurance racing Hypercars competing both in the FIA WEC and IMSA in North America, which will be introduced from 2030.  The new framework will provide greater cost-efficiency for manufacturers to compete in endurance racing championships and events globally, boosting potential participation and increasing the spectacle for motor sport fans.   With interest in FIA WEC at levels never seen before, the championship is positioned for continued growth and success over the coming decade. This new deal offers the solid foundation needed to secure its future, marking a milestone moment in the history of FIA WEC.    Mohammed Ben Sulayem, President of the FIA , said:  “This is not simply an agreement, it is a vital step forward for racing that will secure the future of the FIA World Endurance Championship for years to come.     “This is a deal built for the future, a deal of the century, one that strengthens the collaboration between the FIA and ACO, a relationship that dates back over 120 years, and sets the championship up for a decade of record growth that will deliver real benefits to fans, drivers, teams and manufacturers.     “It has been an honour to play a part in the collaboration that has helped usher in this golden age of endurance racing. I look forward to continuing our work alongside President Pierre Fillon and his team as we build on this momentum and shape an even stronger future.”     Pierre Fillon, President of the Automobile Club de l'Ouest , said: “ We are delighted to see the agreement between the FIA and the ACO extended, reinforcing the strong and long-standing relationship that has been at the heart of the FIA World Endurance Championship since its creation in 2012. This partnership has been built on trust, shared ambition, and a common commitment to the development of endurance racing.      “Together, the FIA and the ACO have created a solid foundation for the continued success and international growth of the championship, and we look forward to writing the next chapter of this remarkable collaboration. Finally, I would like to thank FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem for the great relationship we have built.”      Alberto Villarreal, General Manager at the FIA , said:  “The FIA World Endurance Championship is stronger and more popular than it has ever been before, with a growing and evolving fanbase, and an impressive roster of top-tier global auto-manufacturers.      “The agreement announced today underlines the investment in the championship from both the FIA and the ACO, and our commitment to continue bringing the sport to new audiences. It is a pivotal moment in the history of FIA WEC, and provides the foundation and stability needed for the championship’s ongoing success.”      Frédéric Lequien, CEO of the Le Mans Endurance Management, the promoter for the FIA World Endurance Championship , said:  “This agreement comes at an exciting time for the FIA World Endurance Championship. The championship is experiencing exceptional momentum, with growing engagement from manufacturers, teams, partners, media, and fans around the world. The extension provides a strong framework to build on this growth, further strengthen the global appeal of the WEC and continue to deliver a world-class championship at the forefront of endurance racing. We are looking forward to an ambitious and exciting future for the FIA WEC.”     -   Notes to Editors     The renewed agreement between the FIA and the ACO follows three other significant long-term agreement announcements since July 2025:      FIA and Formula E sign landmark extension to power Formula E World Championship for another 10 years, announced in July 2025 –  information here        Multi-year Concorde Governance Agreement between the FIA, Formula 1 Group and all 11 race teams, announced in December 2025 –  information here        “Deal of the Century” for FIA World and European Rally Championships in July 2026 –  information here         These announcements form part of the FIA’s strategic investment in the future of motor sport, as it continues its mission to grow participation in the sport and provide a safe and accessible platform for all.      The FIA has seen a radical transformation since 2021, and earlier this year  announced  that it had delivered its strongest set of financial results in a decade in 2025, with an operating profit of €6.7m. It also reported an exceptional gain of €20m through the Formula E contract extension.    About the FIA  The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) is the governing body for world motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations globally. It is a non-profit organisation committed to driving innovation and championing safety, sustainability and equality across motor sport and mobility.   Founded in 1904, with offices in Paris, London and Geneva, the FIA brings together 246 Member Organisations across five continents, representing millions of road users, motor sport professionals and volunteers. It develops and enforces regulations for motor sport, including six FIA World Championships, to ensure worldwide competitions are safe and fair for all.    About the ACO   Founded in 1906, the Automobile Club de l’Ouest (ACO) is the creator and organiser of major motorsport events: the first Grand Prix in history in 1906, followed by the 24 Hours of Le Mans starting in 1923. The ACO has also been the organiser and promoter of the FIA World Endurance Championship (FIA WEC) since 2012 and the creator of continental series: the European Le Mans Series (2004) and the Asian Le Mans Series (2013). The ACO organises the 24 Hours of Le Mans Motorcycle Race, the 24 Hours of Le Mans Karting, the 24 Hours of Le Mans Truck Race, and the French Motorcycle Grand Prix on its Le Mans circuits…   The 24 Hours of Le Mans serves as a true technological laboratory focused on automotive innovation. It is in this spirit that the ACO continues to evolve. Sustainable mobility - embodied in particular by MissionH24, which aims to introduce hydrogen to the 24 Hours of Le Mans - is a key objective for the ACO.   Since 2024, the ACO has held the FIA’s 3-star environmental accreditation and is ISO 20121 certified, the benchmark for responsible event management. In September 2024, the 24 Hours of Le Mans circuit was also voted “France’s Favourite Monument.”    About FIA WEC  The FIA World Endurance Championship (FIA WEC), created in 2012 by the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA) and the Automobile Club de l’Ouest (ACO), represents the undisputed pinnacle of the long-distance discipline.   Bringing together the world’s leading manufacturers, biggest brands, top drivers and most successful teams, FIA WEC races around the globe, pushing the limits of speed, performance and durability while encouraging ever-greater feats of strategic skill. If the fast and fearless drivers are the heroes, then the cars are the stars, from their cutting-edge technology to their dynamic design. And then, of course, there is the sound of the engines – that uncompromising, unadulterated roar.   The cornerstone of the calendar is the iconic 24 Hours of Le Mans, an event born in 1923 that continues to serve as the ultimate test for manufacturers seeking to prove their mettle – but every race has its own character, challenges and pitfalls. As a series with a proud history, a compelling present and a thrilling future, FIA WEC remains endurance racing’s global benchmark, continuously setting the standard in the sport and inspiring generations to come. title: FIA Asia Pacific Congress to Bring Member Clubs Together in the Philippines to Advance Mobility and Motor Sport Across the Region
summary: Members news    The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide, will be hosted by the Automobile Association Philippines (AAP) in Boracay in the Philippines for its Asia Pacific Congress next week, bringing together FIA Member Clubs from across the region.  From 29 September to 1 October, 120 delegates from Member Clubs across Asia and the Pacific, will unite in Boracay for three days of collaboration, innovation and knowledge sharing. Throughout the week, attendees will discuss priorities to advance safe and sustainable mobility for road users and drive greater motor sport accessibility.  The Asia-Pacific region is one of the FIA's most diverse and dynamic, spanning some of the world's fastest-growing mobility markets and an expanding motor sport community. The Congress will provide Member Clubs with an opportunity to share expertise and develop practical solutions which respond to the specific needs of their members and communities.  Across mobility, discussions will focus on road safety, innovation, sustainable and accessible transport, tourism and the changing needs of road users, building on the FIA's work to support Clubs in delivering meaningful impact at a national and regional level.  Motor sport sessions will explore opportunities to increase participation, strengthen grassroots competition and create more accessible pathways into the sport, supporting the FIA's ambition to make motor sport more affordable and accessible around the world.  The programme will also showcase the work and innovation of FIA Member Clubs across Asia-Pacific, providing a platform to share successful initiatives which can be adapted and scaled across the region.   H.E. Mohammed Ben Sulayem, President of the FIA, said:   "The Asia-Pacific region is central to the future of both mobility and motor sport, and our Member Clubs are at the heart of that progress.   From improving road safety and embracing innovation to creating new opportunities for people to participate in motor sport, our Clubs are delivering real impact for their communities.    "The FIA Asia Pacific Congress gives us an important opportunity to bring that expertise together, share ideas and strengthen collaboration across one of the most diverse and dynamic regions in our Federation.    "I thank our hosts the Automobile Association Philippines, and President Joe Ferreria, for welcoming the FIA family to Boracay and look forward to another productive Congress."    FIA Region II President and President of host club the Automobile Association Philippines, Augustus ‘Joe’ Ferreria said:   "The strength of this region comes from the diversity, knowledge and ambition of our Member Clubs. Bringing our community together in the Philippines gives us the opportunity to learn from one another, identify shared challenges and develop solutions that can support Clubs across the region.    "The Asia Pacific Congress is an important moment for us to build on the progress already being made and ensure our Clubs have the tools, knowledge and connections they need to continue growing.    "We are proud to welcome the FIA and our fellow Member Clubs from across Asia-Pacific to the Philippines.”   The Congress follows a period of significant activity for the FIA across the region.  The FIA has expanded its  Safe Mobility 4 All & 4 Life  programme into Asia-Pacific, supporting Member Clubs and authorities with training and practical tools to improve road safety, while initiatives including the  FIA Innovation Challenge  continue to showcase Club-led solutions which can be shared and scaled across the Federation.  Across motor sport, the region continues to play an important role at every level of competition, from grassroots participation and regional championships through to the FIA's major World Championships with Malaysia set to host the Bahrain Grand Prix in the days following the congress.  The FIA Member Club structure forms the backbone of the federation’s governance and operations, with each full Member Club holding voting rights across the FIA’s elections and regulatory decisions. Clubs are grouped into two primary categories, with some serving in both roles:   Mobility Clubs – provide mobility services and represent the interest of road users, with a focus on road safety, travel and tourism, consumer rights, and sustainable mobility  National Sporting Authorities (ASNs) – govern and develop motorsport at a national level, are responsible for sporting events, issuing licenses, and engagement across regulations   Within the FIA there are four Mobility Regions and 6 sport zones. The FIA Asia Pacific Congress will welcome Member Clubs from across the region. The global FIA Membership is comprised of 246 clubs across five continents, connecting over 80 million members.      -ENDS-      For media enquiries please contact:   Geri Sherwin, Director of Presidential and Mobility Communications:  gsherwin@fia.com   George Mitchell, Mobility Communications Officer:  gmitchell@fia.com        About the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile    The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) is the governing body for world motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations globally. title: ‘DEAL OF THE CENTURY’ PAYING DIVIDENDS FOR FIA WORLD RALLY CHAMPIONSHIP AS FORD RACING CONFIRMS ITS RETURN FROM 2028
summary: Sport news The Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide, has today welcomed Ford’s announcement that it will return to the FIA World Rally Championship with a full factory programme from 2028 and develop an all-new Rally1 car under the FIA’s WRC27 technical regulations for 2029.  Ford’s return to the championship will mark its first full works programme in the FIA WRC since 2012 and comes at a significant moment in the championship’s development. With new technical regulations arriving in 2027, increased investment under new ownership and plans to expand the WRC’s presence in key markets including the United Kingdom and United States, the series is entering a new period of sporting and commercial growth.  The announcement makes Ford the fourth constructor to commit to developing a car under the FIA’s new WRC27 technical regulations. Designed around safety, affordability, flexibility and accessibility, the regulations will reduce the cost of competing at the highest level of rallying, with the price of a ready-to-compete car capped at €345,000 in asphalt specification.  From 2028, Ford Racing will become directly involved in its FIA WRC programme alongside long-standing partner M-Sport, before introducing an all-new Rally1 car developed to the WRC27 technical regulations in 2029. The commitment reflects the growing attractiveness of the FIA World Rally Championship to global automotive manufacturers and reinforces the role of FIA World Championships as genuine laboratories for the development, testing and demonstration of future technologies.  Ford’s commitment follows growing interest in the new regulations from both global automotive manufacturers and independent constructors and comes as the championship has recently secured the ‘Deal of the Century’ and enters a new period of commercial development under its recently appointed promoter team.  The growing manufacturer interest also underlines the wider role of the FIA’s World Championships as global platforms for automotive manufacturers to develop and demonstrate new technologies, test solutions in demanding competition environments and transfer knowledge between motor sport and road-going vehicles.  Ford’s return to the WRC also forms part of an expanding global motor sport programme. The Blue Oval returned to the FIA Formula One World Championship in 2026, competes in the FIA World Rally-Raid Championship and is preparing to return to the top category of the FIA World Endurance Championship in 2027, having already launched its LMGT3 programme. Its WRC programme will give Ford a presence across four FIA World Championships from 2028.  Ford has played a major role in the history of the FIA World Rally Championship, with cars including the Escort, Sierra, Focus, Fiesta and Puma competing across more than five decades of international rallying.   FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem, said : “Today’s announcement represents another significant moment for the FIA World Rally Championship. With a new promoter in place, three constructors already committed to the new technical regulations, and now Ford confirming its return as a full works manufacturer, there is real momentum behind the championship’s next era.  “Ford is one of the great names in motorsport and its commitment to FIA World Championships continues to grow. The manufacturer returned to Formula 1 this year, is competing at the highest level of the FIA World Rally-Raid Championship, will return to the top category of the FIA World Endurance Championship in 2027, and from 2028 will once again compete as a works manufacturer in the WRC. That will give Ford a presence across four FIA World Championships and demonstrates the importance it places on motor sport as a global platform, and laboratory, for its brand, products and technologies.  “I had the privilege of driving for Ford during my own career, so welcoming them back is a particularly special moment for me. The WRC continues to grow, and this long-term commitment from such an iconic manufacturer is a testament to the strength of the championship.”   Jim Baumbick, President of Ford Europe, said:  “Rallying is where Ford’s character faces its toughest test, and where generations of fans come to share the thrill of seeing a car take on the impossible. We want our next generation of European vehicles to carry that same unapologetic spirit. Responsive, confidence-inspiring, and rewarding to drive on the roads people use every day.”   Mark Rushbrook, Global Director, Ford Racing, said:  “As we celebrate 125 years of Ford Racing, our 50-year legacy in the WRC stands out as one of our proudest because of its direct connection to the fun and exciting cars that came from that. We can’t wait to compete again in rally racing in 2028 and beyond.”   Eric Boullier, CEO of WRC Promoter, said: “ Ford’s decision to return to the FIA World Rally Championship as a full factory team is fantastic news. The brand has an extraordinary history in rallying and has been part of some of the sport’s most memorable moments. More importantly, this renewed commitment to WRC, as part of its extensive global motorsport programme, is a strong statement about the relevance of rallying to one of the world’s leading automotive brands.  “Seeing WRC support both its racing ambitions and the development of future road cars is particularly exciting. We are delighted to welcome Ford back as a full factory team and look forward to this new chapter together.”   Notes to editors:    WRC27 Constructors   Prior to the announcement that Ford will return to the FIA World Rally Championship and develop a new-generation Rally1 car under the WRC27 regulations, three Constructors had already committed to developing cars for the championship’s next technical era:   Toyota has committed to developing a new-generation Rally1 car under the WRC27 regulations.  Project Rally One is developing a new WRC27 car as an independent Constructor project.  WRT Rally1 Spain is developing a new WRC27 Rally1 car as a further independent Constructor project.   Ford’s announcement makes it the fourth Constructor to commit to developing a car under the WRC27 technical regulations.  The WRC27 regulations will come into effect from 2027 and allow both OEMs (Manufacturers) and independent projects to design, homologate and compete with cars at the highest level of the FIA World Rally Championship.  The regulations have been developed to reduce costs, broaden participation and provide long-term stability for the championship. A ready-to-compete WRC27 car in asphalt specification will be capped at  €345,000  ,  significantly lowering the cost of competing at the highest level of world rallying. title: F1 - 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia - Thursday Press Conference Transcript
summary: Sport news  PART ONE – Nico HÜLKENBERG (Audi), Max VERSTAPPEN (Red Bull Racing), Oliver BEARMAN (Haas)    Q: Max, if I can start with you. Very happy birthday for yesterday.   Max VERSTAPPEN:  Thank you.    Q: I hope you managed to enjoy it. We’re back at the site of your second win in Formula 1. What are your memories of racing here?   MV:  Yeah, good question. I mean, to be honest, I walked into the paddock and I had no idea where I had to go, so it’s been a long time. I always enjoyed racing here because I think I really liked the track layout. It was not very straightforward because there was always high degradation, hot in general, so quite uncomfortable in a way, of course, to drive, physically. They are great, great memories but, yeah, had to get into the paddock, I had to get used again. It’s been a bit too long.    Q: In the last three Grands Prix, you alone have outscored Ferrari and McLaren as teams. Is it a sign of improvements in the car? We haven't had a proper wet session this season yet, both when it comes to the tyres that drivers complain about a lot, but also the '26 cars and some of the measures that the FIA has taken, are you confident that everything is in good shape if it ends up wet here?   PG:  I think out of any track in the season, if one is good for wet, it's probably here. So, you know, you'll ask me about Vegas in crazy cold conditions and, well, still could happen there. It was probably going to be definitely more tricky. But here the track's really rough, it's really hot, there's a bit of elevation, so it should be pretty good to clear the track in terms of water quantity. So I think it will be fine. But I think the only time I tried was, you know, in January in Silverstone, which was horrendous, and then in Magny-Cours with extremely cold conditions, which didn't feel good at all. But I expect it to be in a much better place here.    Q: (Adam Cooper – Adam Cooper F1) For Lance and Pierre, you both know Esteban really well. Are you a bit disappointed to see him without a drive for next year, and how good is he at this stage in his career? Lance, you can take that first.   Lance STROLL:  Yeah, I mean, Formula 1's not always fair and, you know, sometimes you're in situations where it's just s**t. And, you know, that's kind of, I think, the situation he's in. I think he's demonstrated over the years that, you know, he's been great in Formula 1 and he's had a lot of good results. So, you know, it definitely sucks for him. And all I can say is I really hope he bounces back and he finds himself in a good situation in the near future. If that's here, if that's somewhere else, if that's, you know, whatever. I just, you know, only wish him the best. You know, he's a great driver and, like I said, he's demonstrated that in Formula 1, not just in Formula 1 but all of his junior years. I was racing in Prema in a similar time to him in our junior career, and I was in F4 and he was in F3, and, you know, he was winning all those races and stuff. And even when we were in karting together, he was always really quick. And yeah, so I only wish him the best.     Q: Pierre, your thoughts?   PG:  Yeah, I mean, I can only agree with Lance. It's a tricky situation, to say the least, and I think at the end of the day it should not take away the almost 200 starts he's had in Formula 1. So I don't think many drivers have achieved that in their career, and it is still something to be very proud of. And in terms of performance, you know, at the end of the day the results speak for themselves. He didn't have the easiest of seasons this year, but it’s not all down to him. And yeah, he's achieved a lot in his time in F1.    Q: (Adam Cooper – Adam Cooper F1) For all three of you, several of your colleagues have just had a boys' holiday together on an island. Were any of you invited, or is the idea of a few days with a bunch of racing drivers a bit of a nightmare? Arvid, you take that one first.   AL:  I didn't get the invite, but honestly, my dream few days off is not with other drivers.    Q: Lance, same?   LS:  Same, yeah.    Q: Did you get the invite and would you have gone?   LS:  No.    Q: (  Qui Chao – Tencent Sports) I have questions for all three drivers. Sepang is a very comprehensive track with two long straights and several straight-line modes. Based on simulator runs, how demanding is this track on energy management, and does this layout favour overtaking with this generation of cars? Arvid, would you like to start?   AL:  Yeah, I don't remember the first part of the question. I don't think it'll be too bad with energy. I mean, none of us have driven here for a while, so I don't think we really know, but I don't think it'll be too bad. I think it will be a more normal experience. And then overtaking difficulty, I think, will actually be on the easier side. And I also think the boost will be relatively powerful on this track because of the layout. So I think, yeah, we'll go towards good racing and lots of overtaking opportunities.    Q: Pierre, your thoughts?   PG:  Yeah, same. Should be good for overtakes and energy, to be fair, I can't really... Yeah, I'll see tomorrow.    Q: Lance, anything to add?   LS:  No.    Q: (Ronald Vording – Motorsport.com) It's one for Pierre, but the others can add if they want to. Fernando said a couple of times in recent weeks that he still has hopes for more regulation changes going into next year. He proposed something in Baku to get some more natural speed traces again and reach a top speed towards the braking zones. Do you think that more is needed, or are you happy to first try what's in place for '27 now?   PG:  I mean, I'm not fully aware of all the changes. I know some of them, which are definitely heading in the right direction. I think overall we've just got to find a way to fine-tune with the tools we have. And I think we all agree we need to make it better. I don't think anyone's fully satisfied with what we've got at the minute. And, I mean, we have a couple of months before starting 2027, and I think anything that can be done with what we've got at the minute needs to be done to improve drivability and improve racing. We're going to enjoy it more at the wheel and I'm sure people will enjoy it as well more from the outside.    Q: Are you giving constant feedback?   PG:  I think, to be fair, with the FIA and F1 it's been a very good relationship in terms of being honest with what we have now. We have a common goal of making F1 better for everyone and they've received our feedback very well, whether it's good or bad. I think we're always very straight with them, for the only goal of making our sport better.    Q: (Adam Cooper – Adam Cooper F1) For all three of you, what are your thoughts on potentially racing at Imola in December? title: A Lifesaving Call, a Mobility Lifeline, and a Solar-Powered Guardian | Region II Champions Announced for FIA Innovation Challenge 2026
summary: Mobility news The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide, has revealed the Region II (Asia-Pacific) Champions of the FIA Innovation Challenge 2026, celebrating the projects that are driving mobility solutions across the Asia-Pacific Region.   Announced as Region II Champions at the FIA Asia-Pacific Congress in Boracay, Philippines, were FIA Member Clubs:     Royal Automobile Club of Victoria (RACV, Australia; Member of the Australian Automobile Association) for ‘ Asure eCall ’, an integrated technology which automatically triggers an emergency call after a crash.       Automobile Association of Ceylon (AAC, Sri Lanka) for ‘ AAC Mobility Lifeline ’, which transformed it’s 24-hour call centre into a national mobility coordination hub in response to Cyclone Ditwah.       AAC received a second award for its ‘ Solar-Guard ’ LED blinker system, giving drivers advanced warning about potential hazards at high-risk locations.     Now in its third year, the FIA Innovation Challenge has seen Member Clubs throughout Region II reinforcing their commitment to supporting individuals and businesses with solutions for safer, more sustainable, and more affordable mobility.    Intelematics and its parent organisation, the RACV, are leveraging the technology of connected vehicles to trigger rapid emergency calls and responses in the event of a crash, while the AAC has showcased how working with its mobility partners supported national resilience and recovery following Cyclone Ditwah. The AAC is also proactively preventing crashes with a solar-powered early-warning system.   H.E. Mohammed Ben Sulayem, President of the FIA said: “ Congratulations to all our Region II Champions and thank you to every Member Club who has continued innovating for road users across the Asia-Pacific Region.     “The projects submitted this year have highlighted the real difference our Clubs can make in times of crisis and how constant innovation is helping us to reduce the risk of crashes and save lives on the road.”    Tim Shearman, FIA Deputy President for Automobile Mobility and Tourism said:  “We are a global network, but it’s the local knowledge of our Mobility Clubs that helps us meet the unique needs of road users everywhere.      “Innovation in mobility is how we improve the lives of road users, and our Region II Champions have embodied that spirit and showcased new solutions that can make a difference locally and across the FIA Network.”    Augustus ‘Joe’ Ferreria, FIA Region II President said:  “Mobility in FIA Region II is diverse and unique and complex, and so are our challenges, so our Mobility Clubs have to work hard to ensure they are always there for the road users they support.     “Our Region has seen the devastating consequences of extreme weather and dangerous roads, and I am so proud to see how these projects have put our Mobility Clubs at the heart of the solution for everyone on the road.”    The FIA Innovation Challenge is an annual contest promoting and celebrating impactful and scalable business and services projects from Member Clubs in the four global Mobility Regions across the FIA Network (Asia Pacific / Europe, Middle East and Africa / North America / South and Central America).    Three champions will be selected from each of the four Mobility Regions, with a global judging panel selecting one Global Winner from each Region, who will receive their awards at the FIA General Assemblies week in Shanghai, China, in December.    The Winning Submissions:    Before the Sirens | Reimagining Connected Crash Response ( RACV, Australia )    Roads in Australia present unique challenges where crashes may occur in remote locations, dangerous environments, and may be hours from the nearest ambulance. Intelematics and its parent organisation, the RACV, have developed the ‘Asure’ connected vehicle platform to trigger an immediate response from connected vehicles when a crash occurs, even if the occupants are unconscious. By automatically transmitting a call with critical data to trained call centre staff, Asure allows for rapid assessment and engagement with emergency services. Intelematics has now expanded Asure into the New Zealand market and supports over 1 million vehicles.   Rob Finney, General Manager, Intelematics said:  “Being involved in a crash is one of the most frightening and dangerous situations a person can experience. Add to that being potentially hundreds of kilometres away from help and unable to make a call, and you have a scary scenario that unfortunately some road users have faced on our regional roads.      “We built Asure so the call for help starts the moment a crash happens, not when someone happens to drive past. Our agents have the crash data within seconds and get it to emergency services quickly and accurately, so help can be on its way sooner. Being recognised by the FIA is a proud moment for our team and the partners who helped shape this platform.”     AAC Mobility Lifeline | Beyond the Call of Duty ( AAC, Sri Lanka )    Cyclone Ditwah struck Sri Lanka in November 2025, causing major disruption for mobility across the country. In response, the AAC activated ‘AAC Mobility’, transforming its 24-hour call centre into a national mobility coordination hub. With a 200% increase in emergency calls, the AAC guided road users, rescue services and evacuees through flooded roads and landslides to safety. Alongside 60 staff, over 135 volunteers, and 50 vehicles, the AAC also mobilised its network of more than 160 accredited garages, demonstrating the importance of local partnerships to support nationwide resilience and recovery during a crisis. As part of its ongoing efforts, AAC has contributed Rs. 25 million to the President’s Fund to support the Government Policy on “Clean Sri Lanka” towards those affected by Cyclone Ditwah.   Dhammika Attygalle, President of the AAC said:  “Extreme weather events are becoming more common, creating uncertainty and increasing risks for road users. So having a network ready to respond when they need us most is vital.     “Cyclone Ditwah showcased the vulnerability of our roads to extreme weather but also demonstrated the power of our partnerships in Sri Lanka. Our people and our community are the driving force behind AAC Mobility Lifeline and our road to recovery.”      Solar-Guard Road Safety Blinking System | Flash to Stop the Crash ( AAC, Sri Lanka )    Sharp bends and hilly terrain coupled with limited visibility and delayed reaction time make Sri Lanka’s highways the site of frequent crashes. To proactively reduce these risks, the AAC, in collaboration with the Road Development Authority, created a solar-powered advanced-warning system, introducing LED blinker lights to high-risk areas. With 24-hour, autonomous visual alerts improving driver awareness, the ‘Solar-Guard’ system is reducing crashes while operating sustainably without dependence on the grid.   Dhammika Attygalle, President of the AAC said:  “Limited visibility on hazardous roads puts drivers at increased risk of being involved in a crash, so finding ways to proactively prevent these incidents from occurring in the first place is essential for protecting road users.     “Through this solar-powered system, we have implemented a sustainable solution to increase visibility for road users in hazardous areas at all times to reduce crashes and save lives.”           -ENDS-        For media enquiries please contact:      George Mitchell, Mobility Communications Officer:  gmitchell@fia.com         Laure Mercier Roussel, Head of Mobility Communications:  lmercier@fia.com        About the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile       The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) is the governing body for world motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations globally. title: FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem meets with Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev as Baku Celebrates a Decade of Racing
summary: FIA news His Excellency Mohammed Ben Sulayem, President of the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), met with His Excellency Ilham Aliyev, President of the Republic of Azerbaijan, in Baku today to discuss shared priorities across motorsport and mobility.  The meeting, which took place during the Baku Grand Prix as the city celebrated a decade of racing on its iconic streets, provided an opportunity to discuss Azerbaijan’s continued development as a major international sporting destination, its established position within global motorsport, and opportunities to strengthen cooperation between the country and the FIA.  Azerbaijan has become an important destination on the international sporting calendar, with Baku providing one of Formula 1’s most distinctive city-centre settings and attracting fans and visitors from around the world.  The Presidents also discussed the wider role of mobility in supporting economic growth and connectivity, as well as the importance of road safety and sustainable transport as Azerbaijan continues to invest in its infrastructure and international connectivity.   FIA President, H.E. Mohammed Ben Sulayem said:   “It was a pleasure to meet with His Excellency President Ilham Aliyev and discuss our shared ambitions for the continued development of motorsport and mobility in Azerbaijan.    “The success of Formula 1 in Baku demonstrates what can be achieved through long-term commitment, strong organisation and a clear vision for the role that major sporting events can play in bringing people together and showcasing a country to the world. My congratulations on a fantastic ten years of racing and I look forward to many more.    “Our discussions also extended beyond motorsport. As the global federation for mobility organisations, the FIA is committed to working with governments and our Member Clubs such as the Azerbaijan Automobile Federation to make mobility safer, more accessible and more sustainable. I look forward to continuing our collaboration with our partners in Azerbaijan across these important areas.”   President Ben Sulayem’s visit comes as the FIA continues to strengthen its engagement across the region through its global network of Member Clubs and partners, including the Azerbaijan Automobile Federation and its President Anar Alakbarov.  The FIA has placed significant emphasis on growing motorsport participation and strengthening the pathway from grassroots competition to the highest levels of the sport, while using its global mobility network to advance road safety, sustainable mobility and accessibility. Azerbaijan’s position at the crossroads of Europe and Asia, alongside continued investment in transport and infrastructure, provides opportunities for further collaboration across both pillars of the FIA’s work. title: WEC: Alpine on pole at Fuji after rain leads to qualifying cancellation
summary: Sport news Heavy rain swept across Fuji Speedway ahead of the scheduled start of the LMGT3 qualifying session, which began on time but was red-flagged after François Heriau went off in his #21 VISTA AF Corse Ferrari.  The decision was then taken to cancel the remaining qualifying sessions due to the forecast of heavier rain and fog at Fuji Speedway.  That meant that, in accordance with the regulations, the grid was set according to the best times from the three Free Practice sessions held across Friday and Saturday morning.  Victor Martins’ FP2 time of 1m40.594s ensured that the #36 Alpine will start from pole position, marking the first-ever WEC pole for the A424 Hypercar.  It was a double celebration for the French manufacturer as the #35 car will join its sister Hypercar on the front row, putting Alpine in a strong position to defend last year’s victory at the venue.  Second on the grid should initially have been the #007 Aston Martin Valkyrie, but it was demoted to fourth after receiving a penalty for causing a collision in the morning’s FP3 session.  Starting third on the grid will be the #17 Genesis Magma Hypercar, meaning the Korean manufacturer will begin tomorrow’s race from by far its best-ever starting position.  In the LMGT3 category, the #77 Proton Competition Ford Mustang will start from pole position after setting the fastest FP2 time on Friday afternoon. title: FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem Meets Lebanese President Joseph Aoun to Discuss Shared Motorsport Priorities
summary: FIA news Mohammed Ben Sulayem, President of the FIA, met with Lebanese President His Excellency Joseph Aoun today after attending the Rally of Lebanon, an event he won four times in a distinguished rally driving career which established him as a sporting ambassador for the Arab world.  The meeting at Baabda Palace provided an opportunity to reflect on the continued success of the event, and Lebanon’s position as a rallying stronghold in the Middle East.  Ben Sulayem accepted an official invitation from the Automobile and Touring Club of Lebanon and President Nabil ‘Billy’ Karam to attend the 48th Rally of Lebanon. The fourth round of this year’s FIA Middle East Rally Championship reached its finish at the ATCL in Kaslik, Jounieh last night (Sunday) with victory going to Lebanon’s Roger Feghali and co-driver Joseph Matar.   “I was pleased to meet with President Aoun and discuss our shared priorities for the future of motorsport,”   said FIA President Ben Sulayem.   “The Rally of Lebanon provided me with many great memories during my rally driving career, and I’m thrilled to once again experience the excitement this event creates for competitors and the country’s passionate motor sport fans.”    “The event has a rich history embedded in the origins of Middle East motorsport. It is firmly established as the home for asphalt rallying in the region, and plays a key role in our plans to ensure the long-term future of the FIA Middle East Rally Championship.    “Lebanon has always felt like a special place for me, and I want to thank the ATCL and its President, Nabil Karam, for their warm welcome and hospitality. I’m delighted to have met up again with some of the friends I have made at the club, and across the country over the years.”   Ben Sulayem’s legendary rally-driving achievements brought him widespread recognition, and he was awarded the President’s Cup by Lebanese President Amine Gemayel in 1987, and the Medal of Honour from Lebanese President Emile Lahoud in 1999.  Each of his four victories in the Rally of Lebanon, in 1987, 1991, 1998 and 1999, helped him secure the FIA Middle East Rally Championship title, which he won 14 times overall. He achieved the last three of those victories alongside his long-time co-driver Ronan Morgan.  Beyond his success in Middle East rallying, Ben Sulayem recorded his first overseas win in Turkey in 1991, and secured World Rally Championship Group N victories in Spain and Argentina over the following two years. He retired from competitive rallying in 2002.  In July, the FIA announced a landmark long-term commercial rights agreement for the FIA WRC and FIA European Rally Championship, following the acquisition of WRC Promoter GmbH by Cosmobilis and Park Square Capital. Designed to bring significant new investment into the sport, the biggest deal in the history of these championships supported the FIA’s vision under President Ben Sulayem, who said at the time:  “Rallying is a huge part of my personal story. title: New Book Maps Seven Forms of Online Abuse Threatening Sport
summary: FIA news The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide, and Dublin City University (DCU) announce the publication of "Combating Online Abuse in Sports: The Game Beyond the Screen".    Supported by the FIA Foundation and FIA as part of its United Against Online Abuse initiative, and published by Palgrave Macmillan, the new open-access book challenges the idea that online abuse in sport begins and ends with hateful comments.    Bringing together experts from sport, sociology, media, law, cybersecurity, governance and digital business, it explores seven distinct forms of online abuse and examines how they affect a range of stakeholders including athletes, officials, journalists, organisations and the wider sporting community. The book was edited by Professor Theo Lynn (Dublin City University), Dr. Gary Sinclair (Dublin City University), Dr. Katie Liston (Ulster University) and Professor David Hassan (Ulster University).   The seven forms, most of which go unreported and unrecognised, are:     Toxic content: sustained abuse, threats and targeted pile-ons.       Content leakage: private images, medical records and personal data released without consent.       Overloading: coordinated campaigns that overwhelm accounts, inboxes, phone or other digital channels.       False reporting: malicious complaints or mass-reporting designed to damage reputations, disrupt performance and/or careers, or silence targets.       Digital impersonation: fake profiles, account hijacking, deepfakes and other attempts to assume or manipulate someone’s identity.       Surveillance: intrusive monitoring of movements, training patterns, communications, data or private life.       Lockout and control: attacks or restrictions that remove a target’s access to, or control over, their digital identity and communications.     A central message runs throughout the book: responsibility for tackling online abuse cannot simply be placed on athletes and other targets to become more "resilient". Meaningful progress requires coordinated action, stronger safeguarding, better digital security, greater platform governance and accountability, and coordinated action across sport, government, technology, and civil society.   The book is fully open access, ensuring it can be read, shared and used freely by athletes, sporting organisations, governing bodies, policymakers, platforms and researchers worldwide.    H.E. Mohammed Ben Sulayem, President of the FIA, said:   "The FIA is committed to creating a safer digital environment for everyone in sport. This book, supported through our United Against Online Abuse campaign, provides the evidence base and practical framework that athletes, governing bodies and policymakers need to tackle online abuse in all its forms."     Professor Theo Lynn, Lead Editor and Executive Dean at DCU Business School, said:   “For too long, online abuse in sport has been treated as a problem of hateful comments. It is much bigger than that. Athletes can face deepfakes, leaked personal data, coordinated attacks, surveillance and even the loss of control of their own digital identity. If we cannot recognise these harms, we cannot tackle them. This book gives sport a common language for understanding the threat and a practical basis for action. By making it open access, we want that knowledge in the hands of everyone who can help make sport safer.”​     ENDS    For media enquiries please contact Maria Zander, Corporate Communications Manager:  mzander@fia.com      About United Against Online Abuse (UAOA)    Founded in 2023 by H.E. Mohammed Ben Sulayem, President of the FIA, the United Against Online Abuse (UAOA) coalition is an award-winning global initiative dedicated to combatting online abuse in sport through research, policy advocacy, and collaborative action. UAOA is endorsed by more than 75 governments, sports, academic institutions and technology organisations, and is supported by the FIA Foundation and co-funded by the European Union.      About the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA)    The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) is the governing body for world motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations globally. title: ETRC: Chrome title chase takes centre stage at Jarama season finale
summary: Sport news Defending champion  Mark Taylor  trails  John Newell  by 13 points following an all-action visit to Le Mans last weekend with results in France determining that only British drivers Newell or Taylor can be Chrome champion for 2026.   “The title’s at stake but we just take each weekend as it comes,”  said Newell.  “I might be leading but it’s not job done [in the championship]. It starts again at Jarama, we just reset and go and make sure we have a good Saturday, then we should be on our way. I need to be fast. It’s a technical circuit, a very enjoyable circuit as well with lots of ups and downs where you can pick your places to overtake.”   Taylor, who became Chrome champion for the first time at Jarama last October, said:  “It’s going to be a tight and fun battle to the end. We’re cat and mousing on the points. We’ve just got to keep it on track, keep our fingers crossed and we’ll have no problems, It would be good to win but I don’t think about it. It’s whatever it’s going to be. If you think about it, you’re going to put pressure on yourself and then the mistakes come. In my mind it would be nice to win again, if we don’t, we don’t, no hardship, it’s motorsport and we’ll be back next season and push again.”   Despite winning his eighth overall Goodyear FIA ETRC title* at Le Mans,  Norbert Kiss  has no plans to slow down behind the wheel of his Révész Racing MAN when the season concludes in Spain.   “All the pressure is off, but we don’t lay back, we keep pushing because you’re only worth as much as your last race,”  said Hungarian Kiss.  “Jarama is a circuit I love, it’s been very good for us in the past with some very nice and very important victories. We try to do the maximum as well and enjoy maximum the weekend and enjoy the success of the season.”     Although top end-of-season Goodyear FIA ETRC silverware is out of reach for  Antonio Albacete  and  Luis Recuenco , the Spanish drivers have the honour of racing at home this weekend.  The 39th Grand Prix de España FIA Europeo de Camiones event is also the closest it gets to a home round for Portugal’s  José Eduardo Rodrigues , who made sure of the Goodyear FIA ETRC Young Driver crown* at Le Mans.  Six-time champion  Jochen Hahn  will battle Albacete and  Sascha Lenz  for the runner-up spot in the final Goodyear FIA ETRC title reckoning. Lenz is four points ahead of Hahn with Albacete 13 points adrift.   Lukas Hahn , who has been competing on a race-by-race basis this season, returns for the Jarama showdown. Jochen’s son was a race winner at Autodrom Most in August where he was also the recipient of the Goodyear Wingfoot Award, which is awarded at each round of the Goodyear FIA ETRC.   Steffi Halm  and  René Reinert , plus  Steffen Faas  and  Clemens Hecker  will compete at Le Mans this weekend as will  Luke Garrett  and  Bradley Smith , a double Chrome winner at Le Mans.  Multiple Finnish champion and FIA ETRC race winner  Mika Mäkinen  takes over the IVECO raced by his daughter, Emma, at Nürburgring and Autodrom Most earlier this season.  After banking two Goodyear FIA ETRC Chrome podiums at Circuit Zolder in mid-September,  Jonathan André  will be one to watch in his TotalEnergies-supported MAN.   THE GOODYEAR FIA ETRC IN SHORT  Combining the excitement of truck racing with entertainment, sustainability and technical innovation, the Goodyear FIA ETRC is heavy metal motor sport at its very best, a truly unique spectacle and the pinnacle of global truck competition with 2026 marking the 20th full season since the current format was introduced.  With the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA) assuming full control of the series, the Goodyear FIA ETRC enters an exciting new era in 2026.  As well as continuing to oversee the Goodyear FIA ETRC’s sporting and technical regulations, the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide is taking a more hands-on approach in running the championship.  Areas such as partnerships, calendar development, circuit relations, competitor engagement and paddock operations are all being managed directly by the FIA, part of efforts to strengthen the championship’s long-term growth by covering areas from sporting level to media exposure and sustainability.   SUSTAINABILITY AT THE HEART OF GOODYEAR FIA ETRC  Back in 2021, the Goodyear FIA ETRC became the first FIA-sanctioned motor sport series to switch to fully sustainable biofuel through a partnership with TotalEnergies, which continues in 2026.  All FIA ETRC drivers use Goodyear tyres incorporating 60 per cent sustainable materials, a five per cent increase compared to 2025, achieved through the use of carefully selected ingredients, such as silica produced from waste rice husk ash and carbon black sourced from alternative feedstocks. Goodyear retreads its racing tyres into standard truck tyres, thereby avoiding the practice of disposing of racing tyres.  Italian manufacturer IVECO, which introduced its electric S-eWay as the official Goodyear FIA ETRC pace truck in 2025, also remains a key partner.   CHAMPION KISS AT THE TRIPLE AS RODRIGUES AND SMITH SHINE IN GOODYEAR FIA ETRC   Norbert Kiss celebrated winning the Goodyear FIA European Truck Racing Championship title* for a record-extending eighth time at Le Mans last Saturday before adding two further wins of a dominant season to his tally of 18 by finishing first in both Race 3 and Race 4 in the Sunday sunshine. Despite wrapping up the coveted crown in Race 1, Kiss continued his pursuit of Goodyear FIA ETRC glory during the final day of the 24 Heures Camions weekend at the famous French venue. He set a stunning lap of 2m03.820s around the 4.185-kilometre Circuit Bugatti in second qualifying to bank pole position number 12 of 2026. His qualifying best in 2025 was a 2m04.322s. The MAN-powered Révész Racing driver then secured the Race 3 win by a commanding margin of 8.801s ahead of six-time champion Jochen Hahn with Sascha Lenz finishing third to continue his push for the runner-up spot in the final title standings behind Kiss. But the Hungarian hero left his best to last when he charged through from eighth on the Race 4 reverse grid to win ahead of Chrome star Bradley Smith – who led overall for four laps – and Antonio Albacete. Points scored by Kiss and René Reinert at Le Mans ensured their Révész-Reinert Racing Team won the Goodyear FIA European Truck Racing Championship for Teams* with one round remaining. Having snatched the Goodyear FIA ETRC Chrome points lead from defending champion Mark Taylor by winning the category in Race 2, John Newell edged ahead of his British rival with a second consecutive victory in Race 3 before Smith took the honours in Race 4 having also triumphed in Race 1. Newell finished second with Taylor in third. Heading into the Jarama season showdown, Newell leads Taylor by 13 points. After winning Race 2, José Eduardo Rodrigues’ Le Mans weekend got even better when he wrapped up the Goodyear FIA ETRC Young Driver crown* in Race 3. However, the third-generation competitor from Portugal suffered a frustrating Race 4 when he ran wide and dropped back while running in second place. He recovered to 10th from 14th.   FANS GET THEIR SAY WITH NEW-FOR-2026 GOODYEAR WINGFOOT AWARD   Already presented in several major series, including the FIA World Endurance Championship, European Le Mans Series and the British Touring Car Championship, the Goodyear Wingfoot Award is new to the Goodyear FIA European Truck Racing Championship for 2026 and recognises driver performance and achievement in the Goodyear FIA ETRC. At each of the seven Goodyear FIA ETRC events, a panel of experts from the FIA and Goodyear nominate three drivers following Race 3, based on their overall performance during the race weekend, their sporting behaviour and highlights on track. Fans will then be able to vote for their driver of the weekend via   Instagram   from the shortlist of candidates during Race 4. The winner is announced as part of the live broadcast coverage of Race 4 and presented with the Goodyear Wingfoot Award on the final podium. Norbert Kiss (Misano), Sascha Lenz (Slovakia Ring), Jochen Hahn (Nürburgring), Lukas Hahn (Most), John Newell (Zolder) and Steffi Halm (Le Mans) are the winners so far. GOODYEAR FIA ETRC DRIVERS LOOK AHEAD TO JARAMA Antonio Albacete (Spain):  “For me to race at Jarama is fantastic. It’s my home race, 25 kilometres from where I live. It’s always very good to race there, it’s an old-shape circuit and quite demanding. But I like to be there and I always like to race there. It’s a little bit narrow but it’s good for truck racing. It’s a challenge with some tricky corners and also some fast ones when you come down the hill. It’s demanding and you have the heavy braking before the left-hander. It’s fantastic to win at Jarama, it’s always great, even for the fans. As we are not playing for the championship, sometimes it’s worth to finish eighth for the reverse grid. Jochen [Hahn] and me are winning there the most so there will be a fight for that title.”   Luke Garrett (Great Britain):  “Jarama has always been my favourite track, even when my dad (Ross) was racing. I love Jarama but we just haven’t had any luck there. We’ve never nailed the set-up, but I love the track when it goes up and down, the aggressive surface, the corners and the banking. I always look forward to it, but I just need a little bit of luck. Fingers crossed we’ll get that this year.”   Steffi Halm (Germany):  “I love Jarama. It’s like an old-school track, going up and down. You have some corners you don’t see the exit, so it’s a very tough track but I love driving at Jarama. Sometimes it’s worked very well, but sometimes not. It depends how you get the set-up done for the track. We’ve had some great results in the past, but for sure the most important thing is to have a good qualifying, that’s the reason why we struggled a bit this season, the qualifying was not good enough, so I hope we can finish on the podium in Jarama but not only in the reverse-grid races.”   Luis Recuenco (Spain):  “For me, Jarama is the benchmark circuit. It is the track where I have gained the most experience, it’s where I started racing in 1988, and where I have been able to put everything I have learned into practice. I am Spanish, and the circuit is very close to home. I enjoy every corner, every braking zone and every racing line. I also really enjoy the atmosphere and the people. At the end of the day, we are all from the same city, so there is a very special connection with the spectators. My goal is simply to do the best job possible. I believe that will allow me to achieve better results and, above all, to feel more fulfilled and more in tune with myself as a driver.”   José Eduardo Rodrigues (Portugal):  “Jarama is five hours from my home so it’s my home race and I feel very good in Jarama. Normally I have good results there. This year is no different and I try to push to the maximum. For me the track is not easy but I like Jarama. I’ve raced there many times, so I have a good reference there. Maybe after Zolder it’s my second favourite race track. We have a lot of fans there, Portuguese people, Spanish people so it’s very good for me and I try to be calm and try to do a good result for the fans.”   GOODYEAR FIA ETRC IN SHORT 4x7:  Seven rounds with four races per event (two races each day)  160 kph:  Safety-first approach means a speed limit of 160kph  1200bhp:  Power output of 1200bhp and torque of around 6000Nm  5300:  Minimum required racing truck total weight is 5300 kilograms, with a minimum of 3150 kilograms measured on the front axle  Qualifying format:  For Races 1 and 3 a three-stage qualifying format decides the grid: Q1/Q4: 15 minutes for all drivers; Q2/Q5: 10 minutes for the 12 fastest drivers from Q1/Q4; Q3/Q6: 5 minutes for fastest six drivers from Q2/Q5; grid positions for Races 2 and 4 decided by the results of Races 1 and 3 with the top-eight drivers lining up in reverse order  Titan or Chrome:  Drivers are either categorised as Titan or Chrome depending on their experience and level of success  Titles:  Four FIA titles for Overall and Chrome drivers, Young Driver and Teams  Goodyear Wingfoot Award:  Three drivers are nominated for the public vote on via   Instagram   during Race 4 based on their overall performance, sporting behaviour and highlights on track     GOODYEAR FIA ETRC ROUND SIX ESSENTIALS Venue:  Circuito de Madrid Jarama – RACE, Autovía A-1, km. 28, 28700 San Sebastián de los Reyes, Madrid, Spain  Website:   https://carreradecamionesjarama.es/en/   Date:  3-4 October 2026  Track length:  3.850 kilometres  Turns:  14 (8 right, 6 left)  Direction:  Clockwise  2025 winners:  Norbert Kiss x 2, Antonio Albacete x 1, John Newell x 1  Tickets:  Click   HERE   for more information  In 100 words:  Designed by John Hugenholtz, whose work included Suzuka and Zolder, Circuito de Madrid Jarama is located in San Sebastián de los Reyes, just north of the capital and was Spain’s first permanent circuit when it opened in 1967.
